incidents.vector: AI-assisted phishing-kit-as-a-service ('Outsider') sold by subscription, letting customers spin up fake brand sites to harvest card and bank credentials.
incidents.impact: FBI, Google and Lumen ('Operation Ghost Hook') dismantled the China-based Outsider operation tied to an estimated $1.9B in losses and 3.9M stolen credit cards, seizing core servers, domains and wallets.

incidents.vector: Data breach traced to a software engineer who accessed customer records and subsequently left the country.
incidents.impact: South Korea fined the US-owned retailer $409M (1.7% of 2025 sales) over a 2025 breach exposing personal data of 34M citizens; Coupang says it will appeal.

incidents.vector: Threat actor contacted the agency demanding payment to withhold allegedly stolen data.
incidents.impact: Jamaica's health ministry is being extorted over a claimed data theft; the government says it is still investigating whether a breach occurred.

incidents.victim: Higher education sector (incl. University of Nottingham)
incidents.vector: Zero-day exploitation of Oracle PeopleSoft (CVE-2026-35273, CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated RCE in the Environment Management Hub), followed by MeshCentral C2 and SSH credential-spraying for lateral movement.
incidents.impact: The ShinyHunters extortion group hit 100+ organizations (68% higher education, mostly US) from May 27-Jun 9 and began leaking data; the University of Nottingham confirmed theft of a 'significant amount' of student data (~455,000 records, 40GB claimed).

incidents.vector: Breach of a government agency managing healthcare entitlements; data subsequently posted to online criminal markets.
incidents.impact: Personal information of more than 67M Thai citizens was allegedly stolen; the Thai government has opened a probe after portions appeared on black markets.

incidents.vector: Mass exploitation of CVE-2026-10520, a max-severity (CVSS 10) OS command-injection flaw giving unauthenticated root RCE, weaponized within 24 hours of a public proof-of-concept.
incidents.impact: Shadowserver observed widespread exploitation attempts with at least two instances already backdoored; the appliance's gateway position exposes stored credentials and directory connections. CISA added the CVE to its KEV catalog.

incidents.victim: US companies, NATO governments and Dutch national police
incidents.vector: Stolen session tokens and purchased VPS/domain infrastructure used to authenticate to cloud accounts and harvest bulk email, files and Teams conversations, with proxies masking origin.
incidents.impact: US prosecutors charged Russian national Denis Obrezko for supplying infrastructure to a Kremlin-linked espionage campaign that compromised at least 11 US companies (likely many more) and previously breached the Netherlands' national police.

incidents.vector: Compromise of the lawmaker's Signal messaging account by suspected Russian hackers.
incidents.impact: The FBI notified the Nebraska Republican — a vocal Ukraine supporter and Kremlin critic — that his Signal account had been breached.

incidents.vector: Bulletproof hosting that staged DDoS, proxy/anonymity and disinformation infrastructure for Russian-linked operations, including attacks on Danish government bodies.
incidents.impact: Dutch financial-crime investigators arrested two operators and seized 800+ servers, shutting down the EU-sanctioned Stark Industries successor network; customer data on seized servers was reported lost.

incidents.vector: A 'cybersecurity incident affecting ICT systems' of unconfirmed nature.
incidents.impact: The 1,428-pupil school sent most students home for a second day and remained closed (only exam candidates admitted) while working with NCSC and specialist responders.
A hacktivist group calling itself 'Nullsec Philippines' defaced the official website of the Philippines Senate.

incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-service targeting internet-facing VPNs and firewalls, then rapidly encrypting entire networks within hours; affiliates lured with a 90/10 revenue split.
incidents.impact: 'The Gentlemen' has become the second most active ransomware brand by victim count (332 since mid-2025, 240+ in 2026); researchers tied the administrator to a named individual in Izhevsk, Russia.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack that forced a halt to operational systems.
incidents.impact: Australia's second-largest sugar producer paused cane haulage and milling at two Mackay-region mills at the start of the annual crushing season, disrupting the harvest.

incidents.vector: Custom-developed ransomware and data-theft extortion deployed against more than 1,000 victims across 31 countries.
incidents.impact: Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko pleaded guilty for his role in the Conti operation (which extorted $150M+), including attacks that crippled Tennessee government, police and EMS entities; he faces up to 20 years.

incidents.vector: Social-engineering attempts tricking users into clicking malicious links, plus creation of WhatsApp test accounts and groups, in defiance of a permanent court injunction.
incidents.impact: Meta says it disrupted a new NSO Group targeting campaign and is petitioning the court to hold the sanctioned spyware maker in contempt for violating the 2025 no-hacking injunction.

incidents.victim: Open-source software supply chain (npm: Microsoft Azure SDK, Red Hat packages)
incidents.vector: A self-propagating 'Shai-Hulud' worm pushed through compromised official npm publishing accounts, embedding malicious install scripts that steal credentials and spread machine-to-machine.
incidents.impact: At least 72 Microsoft public repos tied to the Azure Durable Task SDK were reinfected and official Red Hat npm accounts were used to push the credential-stealing worm; npm announced it will block auto-run install scripts by default in v12.

incidents.vector: Repeated intrusions by attackers linked to foreign governments, allegedly concealed from the US government to protect federal contracts.
incidents.impact: A whistleblower lawsuit by IBM's former VP of threat intelligence alleges both companies hid multiple breaches over years and made false security assurances to win and keep federal contracts.

incidents.victim: Obama White House & US Space Force Instagram accounts
incidents.vector: Social-engineering of Meta's AI support assistant, which was tricked into linking a new email to target accounts and issuing a password-reset code (defeated when MFA was enabled).
incidents.impact: High-profile Instagram accounts were briefly defaced with pro-Iran messaging; attackers also hijacked valuable short usernames, prompting Meta to push an emergency patch.
